prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

UKIP Manifesto 2017 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core pitch: UKIP casts itself as the “guard dogs of Brexit,” promising a radical, costed programme without tax rises, funded by £35bn savings (cut foreign aid to 0.2% GNI, scrap HS2, reform Barnett, end EU payments).

Brexit: Six tests before exit is “done”: legal sovereignty (no ECJ/ECHR jurisdiction), full migration and border control (end free movement), full maritime control (200‑mile EEZ; fisheries repatriated), trade sovereignty (leave Single Market and Customs Union; WTO seat and deals), no “divorce bill” and recovery of UK assets, completion by end‑2019. Fisheries: repeal 1964 London Convention, end discards, license limited foreign access temporarily, land all UK‑caught fish in UK, build protection force, regenerate coastal shipbuilding.

Economy/cost of living: Remove VAT from domestic energy and hot takeaway food; scrap green levies and TV licence; remove VAT on sanitary products. Tax: raise personal allowance to £13,500 and 40% threshold to £55k; raise inheritance tax threshold to £500k (aim to abolish); flexible state pension with option for women at 60. Crack down on multinational tax avoidance.

Business/jobs: Cut business rates 20% for small premises; penalise persistent late payers; open public procurement to SMEs; no quarterly tax returns or NI hikes for self‑employed. Require jobs be advertised to UK citizens first; allow preference for under‑25 Brits; protect workers’ rights; enforce minimum/living wage; curb zero‑hours abuse.

Housing: Create a Housing Development Corporation to deliver up to 100,000 factory‑built modular homes annually on brownfield sites for under‑40 first‑time buyers, freehold with resale back to HDC; review housing associations; enable new council housing. Coastal Enterprise Zones with rate cuts, regeneration powers.

NHS/social care: Extra £9bn p.a. for NHS England by 2021/22 and £2bn for social care; lift cap on med school places; free tuition for medical students tied to NHS service; target 10,000 more GPs; more nurses/midwives (restore bursaries; end 1% pay cap ≤Band 6); integrate health and social care under a new department; crack down on ineligible use; regulate managers; end PFIs; guarantee EU health workers’ right to remain. Mental health: +£500m p.a.; 28‑day max wait; school counselling; perinatal access; better hospital liaison.

Education: Grammar school in every town; strengthen technical/vocational routes (German‑style dual training); scrap Key Stage 1 SATs; restore maintenance grants; abolish tuition fees for STEM (and NHS medicine) tied to UK service; improve careers and “employability” skills; protect special schools.

Families/elderly/disabled: Wraparound childcare (8–6); emergency childcare registers; £80m fund to include SEN in early years; shared parenting presumption; more transparent family courts. Maintain triple lock and universal pensioner benefits; reverse social care cuts (£2bn p.a.); dignity code; raise Carer’s Allowance; reform disability assessments; scrap bedroom tax.

Immigration/integration: Target balanced net migration (≈zero) over five years; Australian‑style points plus work permits; 5‑year moratorium on low‑skilled visas; seasonal schemes; 5‑year wait for benefits/non‑urgent NHS; no amnesty; deport foreign criminals. Pre‑A50 EU citizens may remain. One law for all: disband sharia councils; zero tolerance of FGM/forced marriage/honour crime; ban face coverings in public; act against school Islamism.

Law and order: +20,000 police, +7,000 prison officers; restore stop and search; keep/open prisons; deport foreign inmates; tougher sentences (including for corruption); curb prison extremism; repeal 2003 Licensing Act; opt out of European Arrest Warrant.

Defence/foreign: Spend a genuine 2% of GDP plus £1bn/yr uplift; +20,000 personnel; maintain Trident; overhaul procurement; new Veterans’ Administration, housing/jobs guarantees, legal shield for veterans; cautious on interventions; pro‑US/Commonwealth; conditional engagement with Russia.

Trade/aid: “Trade not aid”: abolish DfID; cut aid to 0.2% GNI; focus on emergencies/health/water; UK providers preferred; commission a 500‑bed hospital ship; pursue global FTAs; ready for WTO‑terms EU trade.

Transport: Scrap HS2; oppose Heathrow third runway; remove road tolls; support EV charging; protect diesel owners from new penalties; bolster regional airports; introduce “Britdisc” for foreign vehicles.

Environment/energy/animal welfare: New Environmental Protection Act; protect ancient woodland; brownfield first; cut plastic waste; restore dredging. Repeal Climate Change Act; diversify energy (including shale, nuclear); cut green levies. Farming: UK Single Farm Payment with cap; support small/organic/hill farms. Animal welfare: CCTV in abattoirs; label method of slaughter; ban live export; tougher cruelty sentences.

Democracy/localism: Abolish House of Lords; PR voting; English Parliament; halve Commons to 325; binding citizens’ initiative referenda; scrap postal voting on demand; empower local referenda; committee system in councils; keep council tax low.
